title: Normalized flow decline within dry spells rose after 1997 in 348 southern Australian catchments
abstract: In 348 southern Australian catchments, normalized flow decline from dry day 3 to day 8 rose by 0.0237 after 1997. The joint 95% interval from five-year weather blocks and spatial cells was 0.0083 to 0.0424. The estimate for 2010-2021 was 0.0233 (0.0062 to 0.0427; 331 catchments). A second rain product and a geographic south-east subset gave the same direction. This new within-event signature survives an exact removal of constant discharge scale. It does not identify the cause of annual runoff loss. We match season, prior rainfall and within-era starting-flow rank. The bounded endpoint statistic includes zero flows and is invariant to a positive constant flow multiplier. An earlier southern placebo is near zero; northern controls have no clear pooled rise. Limits include coarse matching, dry-spell duration selection, related rain products, fixed rank and support in the time samples, and no independent store observations. Code, source hashes, source rights, aggregate estimates, uncertainty draws and audits are included.

display.caption: Within-spell normalized flow decline. Bars show conditional spatial 95% intervals. The index is invariant to a constant discharge multiplier.
Joint spatial-cell and five-year weather-block 95% intervals. Rank labels and original cell support are fixed.
